significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive/causal conclusion that steps with excessive information density are disproportionately likely to initiate errors, that a pre-emission pacing signal forecasts those steps, and that selectively lowering their density improves reasoning beyond length-matched computation. This establishes both a cross-task behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing where additional reasoning tokens should be allocated rather than merely asserting that longer reasoning helps—a consequential constraint given work on test-time-compute allocation such as Snell et al., “Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters” (2024). The negative branch is also informative: the claim explicitly says a null would mean researchers should “treat information density strictly as a passive reranking correlate,” ruling out UID-based causal control rather than merely failing to locate a feature; true and false therefore identify distinct states of the world. Topic-substitution check: replacing the specific “information-density bursts” relation with the generic language–intelligence topic would not support this score, because the constraining causal and predictive law would disappear.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: a “pre-step burst probability” that predicts “impending bursts and errors,” and “Burst-Aware Pacing,” a training-free inference-time intervention applied only at flagged steps. These are ex ante handles with an action window before the risky step is emitted, usable by reasoning-system developers and model auditors rather than only for post-hoc interpretability; the asserted scope covers math, logic, multi-hop QA, and clinical reasoning across several model families. Although the pacing direction or probe would need re-extraction, the substantive relation is predicted to survive recalibration: high predicted density should forecast error, and targeted decomposition should outperform random or blanket extra computation, giving downstream systems a transferable allocation rule rather than only a search procedure. Topic-substitution check: the broad language-and-intelligence topic alone supplies neither this predictor nor this inference-time control rule, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handles.
